clue.text: Artist rejected joyless passion

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for artist is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
dour means stern and joyless

explanation.surface: A painter turned down for a cheerless sort of love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or fervour, a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Remedy is to detain criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: The cure is to lock up the crook.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison.

clue.text: Marlene's food full of cholesterol?

definitions.note: Marlene's is read as Marlene is, naming the film star by her surname

parts.note: diet means food eaten
rich food is heavy with fat

explanation.surface: Did the film star eat a fatty diet?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Marlene is the answer, the German-born Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born Hollywood actress and singer, so her surname follows her first name.

clue.text: Without power, capturing German bomb is impracticable

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: unable means lacking the power to do something
the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here as VI

explanation.surface: A powerless attempt to seize a German bomb is doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 'doodlebug' was the flying bomb Germany fired at London in 1944; the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unviable cannot work in practice, so it is not feasible.

clue.text: Catastrophe hit at last in fabulous land

indicators.note: a catastrophe hitting the words wrecks them, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Disaster finally strikes a mythical kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catastrophe hit' is the anagram signal and works on AT LAST IN; the surface makes 'at last' seem to mean 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary island said to have sunk beneath the sea is a fable, so 'fabulous' here means belonging to myth.

clue.text: Instruction's not to stay in contact-it's risky

definitions.text: Instruction's not to stay in contact
definitions.meaning: an order to make contact briefly and then leave

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally orders a brief contact and departure, and idiomatically means precarious or uncertain.

clue.text: Wood and mineral found on the land

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Timber and minerals discovered on dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or towards dry land rather than at sea.

clue.text: Not good enough? I can't help that

definitions.meaning: a dismissive reply meaning that is a pity but nothing can be done

explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means excessively poor, and as a retort it shrugs off a complaint.

clue.text: Time of year for one putting two and two together?

definitions.text: one putting two and two together
definitions.meaning: one who adds figures, a person who sums

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the warmest season and, read as a coined noun, someone who does arithmetic.

clue.text: A number of jurymen-22?

definitions.meaning: a full jury in England is made up of a dozen people
the answer at 22-across is the hour when the clock strikes a dozen

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a cross-reference: the late hour at 22-across is 12 o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury traditionally has a dozen members, and the hour at 22 is twelve o'clock, so both senses are the same number.

clue.text: Husky encouragement to take space to expand rapidly

parts.note: mush is the call a sled driver gives to urge on huskies
room means space

explanation.surface: Cheering on a sled dog to take up more room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like an adjective for a hoarse voice, but it is the sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread suddenly, like the fungus springing up overnight.

clue.text: It forms part of cod or salmon

definitions.text: It forms part of cod or salmon

indicators.note: forms part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fish anatomy fact: something belongs to cod and salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'It' cannot stand for a fin on its own; the whole clue defines the answer, as the fin on a fish's back forms part of cod or salmon, so this is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fin on a fish's back is called this, and cod and salmon both have one.

clue.text: Scarcity of footwear bearing right label

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the footwear holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a shoe is footwear
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A lack of shoes with the right price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or deficiency, the same as a scarcity.

clue.text: A drop in the ocean

parts.note: looks like the idiom for a trivial amount, but is read literally as a spacecraft falling into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A space capsule returning to Earth parachutes down onto the sea at the end of its flight.

clue.text: Delight just to touch a snooker ball

parts.note: to tickle is to touch very lightly
pink is one of the coloured balls in snooker, the cue game played on a large table

explanation.surface: Barely touching a ball on the snooker table brings pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled pink is to be greatly pleased, so the phrase used as a verb means to please enormously.

clue.text: Mad excitement-secure the apartments above

indicators.note: in a down clue above means this piece is written first, over the other

parts.note: flats are apartments
to pin is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: Frenzy as the residents lock up their apartments upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flat spin is to be in a state of panic or agitation.

clue.text: Lent is well on

definitions.meaning: paid money ahead of time, as a loan
far along, at a late stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the season before Easter but is the verb: money lent is paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lent ahead is a loan paid early, and something well along is at a late stage.

clue.text: Germs are terrible in Wordsworth's home

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Microbes run riot in the poet's house.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASMERE is a village in England's Lake District where the poet William Wordsworth lived at Dove Cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet William Wordsworth lived in this Lake District village and is buried there.

clue.text: The hell with plane-he's in the air without one

definitions.text: he's in the air without one

parts.note: hang it is an old exclamation meaning the hell with it
a glider is an engineless plane

explanation.surface: Damn the aeroplane: this flier soars without one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang it!' is a mild British oath; the flier on a kite-like wing is airborne without any plane at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A person flying a light kite-like wing stays aloft without an aircraft, so is airborne with no plane.

clue.text: Show myself accustomed to result of 14 operation

parts.note: showing oneself as being, I am
used means accustomed, as in used to it

explanation.surface: I prove I am used to the outcome of being tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer at 14-across: being tickled pink leaves one entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Being delighted by tickling leaves one entertained and smiling.

clue.text: Fix notice covering fair

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means lying on top, so the notice is written first

parts.note: AD is an advertisement, a notice
just means fair

explanation.surface: Repair the notice that hides the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter something slightly to set it right.

clue.text: One asleep has this for his breakfast?

definitions.meaning: a smoked herring is a traditional British breakfast dish

explanation.walkthrough: A kip is British slang for a sleep; the smoked herring is a classic British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper on a kip and a smoked herring eaten at breakfast share the word.

clue.text: Sort of blue at this late hour

definitions.meaning: a very dark navy shade is named after the darkest part of the night

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a dark navy colour and twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: Light beams on the way, for those that are lost?

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the beams follow the way

parts.note: ST is street, a way
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Shafts of light along the road guide wanderers home.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are animals or people that have wandered off and are lost.

clue.text: Modelling for him you might end up bust

definitions.text: Modelling for him you might end up bust

parts.words: Modelling for him you might end up bust
parts.note: reads like sitting for a fashion photographer and going broke, but bust means a carved head and shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: An artist who carves figures may turn a sitter into a statue of head and shoulders.

clue.text: Native American is every year in pain

indicators.note: in tells us the yearly abbreviation sits inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
PA is per annum, Latin for every year

explanation.surface: An Indigenous person suffers pain each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Remove from high chair and change other end

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Lift the toddler out of the high chair and change the other end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'high chair' is a throne, not a baby's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone is to depose a monarch, removing them from the throne, the highest seat.

clue.text: Nervous that spun coin never lands thus?

definitions.meaning: a tossed coin falls heads or tails, and practically never stands upright on its rim

explanation.definitionFit: To be jumpy is to be on tenterhooks, and a coin balanced upright rests on its rim.
